narratives.name: Opportunity Health Through Multi-Dimensional Qualification
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC transforms opportunity management from intuition-based assessment into structured evidence-based health checks.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise sales organizations pursuing complex technology opportunities must track not just the commercial transaction but the underlying qualification health across multiple interdependent dimensions. Without a structured framework for assessing opportunity viability, pipeline forecasts rely on subjective confidence rather than evidence-based qualification, and the largest, most consequential deals advance through stages without adequate scrutiny of business need, buyer authority, competitive positioning, or procurement readiness.

MEDDPICC transforms opportunity management from intuition-based assessment into structured, multi-dimensional health checks by scoring each of eight qualification dimensions at cumulative Good, Better, and Best levels aligned to Red Hat sales stages. The methodology recognizes that MEDDPICC dimensions do not follow a rigid sequential order and instead uses sales stage context to determine which letters require focus at any given point, while maintaining that Economic Buyer and Champion engagement are continuous throughout the entire cycle. The Global Bookings Pipeline Procedure reinforces this discipline by requiring completed scorecards for threshold opportunities in Commit and Best Case forecast categories.

Organizations that systematically track opportunity health through the MEDDPICC framework achieve measurably improved pipeline predictability because deals with consistently high scores across all dimensions represent genuinely committed pipeline, while deals with significant gaps in one or more dimensions receive targeted intervention before they become unreliable forecast entries. The AI-augmented coaching model further strengthens opportunity management by reducing full 8-letter reviews to focused 30-minute sessions covering 2-3 AI-prioritized letters, enabling more frequent coaching touchpoints that progressively improve qualification quality without increasing time burden on sellers or managers.

narratives.name: Bridging Pain Identification to Quantified Business Outcomes
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC connects customer pain through the Business Value Framework to defensible financial justification.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise technology opportunities frequently stall or lose momentum because the business case connecting the customer's pain to measurable outcomes remains implicit rather than explicit. Sellers may understand the customer's challenges and may know what improvements the customer desires, but without a structured framework that bridges pain identification to metrics quantification, the value proposition remains an emotional appeal to the customer and an unsubstantiated claim to the Economic Buyer.

The MEDDPICC methodology addresses this through two complementary dimensions -- Identify Pain (I) and Metrics (M) -- connected by the Business Value Framework. Pain identification moves from symptom detection through contextualization to quantification, while metrics progress from understanding goals through ROI definition to value quantification with real numbers. The Business Value Framework explicitly links these two dimensions, creating a three-part narrative: the customer experiences specific, named pain, Red Hat's solution addresses the pain and moves specific KPIs, and the improvement translates to financial value including a per-period cost of delay that creates genuine urgency.

When pain identification and metrics quantification are linked through the Business Value Framework, the value proposition transforms from a vendor assertion into a customer-owned narrative. The customer champion can articulate the value story internally because it is grounded in their own data and expressed in their own strategic language. The Economic Buyer can approve investment because the financial case addresses their specific objectives with transparent assumptions. The cost-of-delay calculation anchors the close date in financial reality rather than arbitrary timelines.

narratives.name: Sustained Economic Buyer Engagement Throughout the Sales Cycle
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC structures the identification and sustained engagement of the budget authority holder.

narrativeContexts.context: In complex enterprise sales, the individual who evaluates the technology is rarely the same individual who has the authority to approve the budget. Account teams that focus exclusively on technical stakeholders often discover late in the deal cycle that the Economic Buyer has different priorities, financial constraints, or approval criteria than those the team has been optimizing for.

MEDDPICC's Economic Buyer dimension provides a structured framework for identifying, understanding, and sustaining engagement with the person who has the power to spend, move, and approve budget. The rubric progression moves from basic identification through understanding the EB's pain and readiness to buy, culminating in sustained active engagement throughout the entire sales cycle. The methodology recognizes that EB engagement is not a single event but a continuous relationship.

When Economic Buyer engagement is treated as a sustained, structured discipline rather than an opportunistic touchpoint, the account team gains the ability to align the entire deal strategy to the EB's financial objectives and decision-making context. Partner relationships with the EB provide additional access pathways and intelligence that strengthen engagement beyond what direct sales contact alone can achieve.

narratives.name: Champion Development as the Connective Tissue of Deal Qualification
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC structures champion identification, validation, and engagement to connect all qualification dimensions.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise technology decisions are influenced through organizational networks where informal power and trust carry as much weight as formal authority. Account teams that treat customer engagement as a series of discrete conversations with individual contacts miss the underlying organizational dynamics that determine whether a deal advances, stalls, or is lost.

MEDDPICC's Champion dimension provides a structured three-axis framework for evaluating potential champions: desire (wants Red Hat to win), influence (has organizational respect and political power), and access (can provide intelligence and connect the seller to key stakeholders). The rubric progressively builds from identifying a favorable person through confirming their organizational influence to engaging a power broker who has EB influence, political power, and technical respect.

A fully developed champion serves as the connective tissue between multiple MEDDPICC dimensions. The champion is the conduit to the Economic Buyer, the source of intelligence about Decision Criteria and Decision Process, the internal advocate who counters competitive objections, and the navigator who guides the seller through organizational complexity. When partner champion engagement is coordinated, the combined network provides coverage that neither party could achieve alone.

narratives.name: Navigating Decision Process and Paper Process for Deal Execution
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC distinguishes and manages the complementary dimensions of how customers decide and how agreements are executed.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise deals frequently experience late-stage surprises when the seller discovers that the customer's buying process involves unexpected steps, unfamiliar stakeholders, or longer timelines than anticipated. Paper process challenges are among the most common causes of deal slippage, particularly when they involve unexpected legal reviews, procurement policies, approval hierarchies, or multi-party signature sequences.

MEDDPICC distinguishes between two complementary D dimensions: Decision Process addresses HOW the customer makes purchasing decisions, while Paper Process addresses the administrative, legal, and procedural steps required to execute the agreement. The methodology emphasizes proactive management through mutual action plans rather than passive observation. Paper Process management requires detailed operational knowledge across four sub-domains: contracting, procurement, legal and compliance, and budget and finance.

Account teams that master both the Decision Process and Paper Process dimensions transform from passive respondents in the customer's buying process into active navigators who manage dependencies, clear bottlenecks, and anticipate risks. The mutual close plan with specific dates, owners, and contingencies provides early warning of process delays and creates accountability for both parties. Partner process integration ensures that multi-party deals account for each party's procurement requirements without creating sequential bottlenecks.

narratives.name: Transforming Deal Qualification Through Structured Multi-Dimensional Assessment
narratives.description: How organizations achieve improved pipeline predictability through systematic MEDDPICC qualification.

narrativeContexts.context: Sales organizations pursuing enterprise technology opportunities face a persistent challenge: subjective deal assessments lead to inaccurate pipeline forecasting, wasted pursuit resources, and missed opportunities to strengthen qualification before competitive threats solidify. Without a shared vocabulary and structured assessment framework, sellers and managers evaluate the same deals through different lenses, creating misalignment that compounds as deals move through the pipeline.

The MEDDPICC framework addresses this by providing eight complementary qualification dimensions -- Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Paper Process, Identify Pain, Champion, and Competition -- each with a cumulative Good/Better/Best scoring rubric and a Rudimentary/Proficient/Exceptional quality assessment. The methodology aligns these dimensions to Red Hat sales stages, creating stage-gate expectations for which dimensions should be substantively addressed at each point in the deal cycle, while recognizing that Economic Buyer and Champion engagement are continuous throughout.

Account teams apply MEDDPICC by systematically evaluating each dimension against the rubric, documenting findings in the MEDDPICC Scorecard within Red Hat Sales Cloud, identifying qualification gaps through the Guidance for Missing Letters framework, and engaging specialist resources to fill those gaps. Sales managers conduct structured deal reviews using the three-phase workflow, optionally augmented by PeopleAI/SalesAI for AI-prioritized focus areas. The Business Value Framework connects Pain Identification to Metrics through a quantified value narrative that creates financial urgency.

Organizations that systematically apply MEDDPICC achieve improved deal qualification accuracy through evidence-based assessment rather than subjective confidence, enhanced pipeline predictability through structured multi-dimensional scoring, increased deal velocity through targeted gap remediation guided by specific coaching, and organizational alignment through a shared qualification vocabulary that enables productive conversations about opportunity health at every level.

narratives.name: Proactive Criteria Shaping for Solution Alignment
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC transforms decision criteria alignment from passive documentation into proactive competitive positioning.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise buyers rarely have fully crystallized evaluation criteria when they begin a technology assessment. Account teams that passively accept whatever criteria the customer presents risk competing on dimensions that favor competitors or that fail to capture Red Hat's strongest differentiators. The Decision Criteria dimension is often the dimension most susceptible to competitive influence because vendors that engage early in criteria definition can shape requirements to align with their own strengths.

MEDDPICC's Decision Criteria dimension reframes criteria alignment as a proactive activity where the seller helps shape requirements. The rubric progression moves from exploration through definition to commitment, securing EB consensus that criteria are being met throughout the process. The methodology emphasizes understanding criteria beyond technical features to include budget expectations, vendor support requirements, implementation capability, and compliance certifications.

When criteria alignment is treated as a proactive shaping activity rather than a passive documentation exercise, the account team creates structural advantage that persists throughout the evaluation process. Partner capabilities strengthen the criteria framework by providing implementation expertise and deployment accelerators that complement Red Hat's technology positioning.

narratives.name: Evidence-Based Competitive Positioning Across Three Threat Categories
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC structures competitive assessment against external vendors, in-house development, and organizational inertia.

narrativeContexts.context: Every enterprise technology deal faces competition even when no other vendor is visibly bidding. MEDDPICC identifies three categories of competition: external vendors offering alternative solutions, the customer choosing to develop a solution in-house using open-source or existing tools, and the customer choosing to do nothing. The most dangerous competitive threat is often organizational inertia combined with the perceived safety of existing approaches.

Mature competitive positioning requires a structured progression from awareness through analysis to active counter-positioning. At the foundational level the account team must identify all three categories. At the analytical level the team must document both advantages and disadvantages with specific evidence. At the positioning level the team must develop numbered competitive advantages tied directly to customer pain points, anticipate competitor counter-messaging, and prepare specific counter-narratives validated by the champion.

When competitive positioning is built on specific, evidence-based arguments rather than assumed superiority, the account team creates a defensible competitive narrative that withstands customer scrutiny and competitor attacks. The champion who validates Red Hat's competitive position becomes an advocate who can counter competitive objections in internal discussions. Partner competitive intelligence provides an additional dimension that strengthens the overall competitive picture.

narratives.name: Progressive Scorecard Maturity as Qualification Evidence
narratives.description: How the MEDDPICC Scorecard progresses through four maturity levels to evidence opportunity health.

narrativeContexts.context: The MEDDPICC Scorecard is the primary evidentiary artifact for opportunity qualification, serving as the single source of truth that sellers, managers, and executives reference when assessing deal health. Without progressive maturity in the scorecard's content, deal reviews lack specificity, pipeline forecasts lack evidence, and coaching conversations lack the structured foundation needed to identify and address qualification gaps systematically.

The scorecard progresses through four levels of maturity corresponding to increasing qualification depth, response quality, and cross-dimensional coherence. At the Initial Assessment level the scorecard exists as a framework with basic entries. At the Qualified Assessment level all eight dimensions have substantive Good-level entries. At the Validated Assessment level responses reach Better and Best scoring with Proficient quality. At the Coaching-Enhanced level the scorecard represents comprehensive deal intelligence with Exceptional quality responses refined through structured coaching.

The progressive maturity of the scorecard directly evidences Opportunity state progression. At its highest maturity level the scorecard provides actionable intelligence for pipeline governance, supports accurate forecasting through evidence-based qualification, and creates a comprehensive knowledge transfer package for post-sale success engagement.

narrativeContexts.context: The gap between qualitative pain understanding and quantitative value articulation is where many deals lose momentum. A seller may empathize deeply with the customer's challenges but cannot translate that understanding into the financial language that Economic Buyers require for investment decisions.

The Business Value Assessment progresses from an initial Pain Hypothesis connecting challenges to KPIs, through a Quantified Impact level with specific financial calculations including ROI, payback period, and cost of delay, to a Validated Business Case that has been reviewed and acknowledged by customer stakeholders.

At its highest maturity the Business Value Assessment provides the customer champion with presentation-ready materials for internal advocacy and provides the Economic Buyer with a business case that addresses their specific financial evaluation criteria. The cost-of-delay calculation transforms the close date from an arbitrary target into a financial milestone.

narrativeContexts.context: Deal reviews without structured preparation and documented follow-through devolve into status updates that consume time without driving qualification improvement. Managers who review deals without data-driven prioritization may focus on dimensions that are already strong while missing the dimensions that pose the greatest risk to deal progression.

The Deal Review Briefing combines the structured preparation workflow from the Deal Review Coaching Guide with AI-augmented prioritization from PeopleAI/SalesAI. At the Pre-Review Notes level the briefing establishes discussion objectives. At the Structured Analysis level it incorporates AI-identified priority letters and contextual coaching questions. At the Action Plan level it provides longitudinal tracking of coaching effectiveness.

The structured briefing enables the shift from 1-hour full 8-letter reviews to focused 30-minute sessions covering 2-3 AI-prioritized dimensions, allowing more frequent coaching touchpoints without increasing time burden and producing specific, owned, time-bound actions that measurably improve qualification quality.

narratives.name: From Seller Tracking Document to Jointly Owned Execution Plan
narratives.description: How the Mutual Close Plan transforms paper process management from reactive to proactive deal execution.

narrativeContexts.context: Paper process surprises are among the most common causes of deal slippage in enterprise sales. When the close plan is treated as the seller's internal tracking document rather than a jointly owned execution plan, critical steps are missed, dependencies go unidentified, and timing risks surface too late for effective mitigation.

The Mutual Close Plan progresses from a Draft Timeline with approximate milestones, through Agreed Milestones with mutually committed dates and stakeholder dependencies, to Active Tracking with live status updates, risk management, and partner coordination. The plan integrates both Decision Process milestones and Paper Process execution steps into a single jointly owned artifact.

The close plan at its Active Tracking maturity transforms the seller from a passive participant into an active navigator who manages dependencies, anticipates timing risks, clears bottlenecks through EB and champion relationships, and coordinates multi-party execution. Proactive steps such as sharing draft agreements to anticipate legal review reduce elapsed time between commercial agreement and contract execution.

narratives.name: Structured Pain Discovery as the Foundation of MEDDPICC Qualification
narratives.description: How probing questions move pain identification from generic awareness to specific, quantifiable business impact.

narrativeContexts.context: Pain identification is the foundational MEDDPICC dimension and the starting point for opportunity qualification. Without well-articulated pain, there is no foundation for metrics quantification, no urgency for the Economic Buyer, and no compelling reason for the champion to advocate.

This activity follows a structured discovery process that moves from broad exploration to specific validation. The seller identifies who is experiencing the pain, explores what approaches have failed, establishes the consequence of not addressing the pain, validates with data wherever possible, and assesses alignment with the deal close date.

Common pitfalls include accepting generic pain descriptions without probing for specificity, failing to identify named individuals experiencing the pain, neglecting to explore the temporal dimension including cost of inaction, and treating pain identification as a one-time activity rather than a progressive deepening.

activities.name: Build Business Value Case

Cost-of-delay per period quantifies the financial consequence of decision postponement

narratives.name: Connecting Pain to Metrics Through the Business Value Framework
narratives.description: How the Business Value Framework bridges qualitative pain identification and quantitative metrics for defensible value cases.

narrativeContexts.context: The MEDDPICC methodology identifies a common failure mode where sellers can articulate either pain or metrics but cannot connect the two into a coherent story. This gap leaves the value proposition vulnerable because the Economic Buyer requires defensible financial analysis and the champion needs materials for internal advocacy.

This activity integrates two complementary MEDDPICC dimensions through the Business Value Framework. The seller identifies customer KPIs, maps Red Hat capabilities to specific KPIs, calculates financial impact with real numbers, quantifies cost-of-delay per period, validates with customer stakeholders, and packages the value narrative for champion internal use.

Common pitfalls include using industry averages instead of customer-specific data, failing to calculate cost-of-delay which removes temporal urgency, treating the value assessment as a seller-only document, and applying the Business Value Framework only to Metrics without connecting it back to strengthen pain articulation.

narratives.name: Sustained Economic Buyer Engagement as a Continuous Discipline
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC structures EB identification and engagement as an ongoing relationship rather than a single event.

narrativeContexts.context: In enterprise sales, the person who evaluates the technology is rarely the person who approves the budget. Account teams that focus exclusively on technical stakeholders often discover late in the cycle that the Economic Buyer has different priorities, constraints, or approval criteria.

Economic Buyer engagement begins with identification leveraging champion intelligence and organizational research. The seller determines single vs co-decision-maker dynamics, establishes the path to engagement, understands the EB's financial objectives, and maintains sustained engagement throughout the cycle with regular touchpoints.

Common pitfalls include assuming a single EB when multiple co-decision-makers exist, relying exclusively on the champion for EB access, treating EB engagement as a late-stage activity, presenting generic value propositions rather than framing the case in the EB's specific financial language, and failing to understand the EB's past investment decisions.

narratives.name: Three-Axis Champion Assessment and Development
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC evaluates champion quality along desire, influence, and access dimensions.

narrativeContexts.context: Not every friendly customer contact is a true champion. A contact who lacks influence cannot drive action regardless of their enthusiasm, and a contact who lacks access cannot provide the organizational intelligence the seller needs to navigate the decision process.

Champion development begins with identifying contacts who meet all three criteria: desire, influence, and access. The seller assesses organizational standing, understands professional and personal motivations at depth, identifies what the champion needs to advocate effectively, and develops coordinated counter-strategies for internal objections.

Common pitfalls include accepting a friendly contact as a champion without validating influence and access, failing to understand the champion's personal motivations, neglecting to equip the champion with specific materials for internal advocacy, and failing to coordinate with partner champion engagement.

narratives.name: Proactive Criteria Shaping for Competitive Advantage
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC transforms decision criteria from passive documentation to active competitive positioning.

narrativeContexts.context: Customers often need help crystallizing their own evaluation requirements. Sellers who passively accept whatever criteria the customer initially presents risk competing on dimensions that favor competitors.

Decision criteria mapping is a proactive activity where the seller helps shape requirements. The seller identifies criteria across technical, vendor support, integration, and compliance dimensions, establishes priority ranking, explores budget expectations with depth, and identifies the budget owner to establish direct contact.

Common pitfalls include treating criteria mapping as passive documentation, neglecting the budget dimension in favor of exclusive technical focus, failing to connect criteria to competitive positioning, and missing the opportunity to shape criteria early before competitors influence requirements.

narratives.name: Transforming Decision Process Navigation from Passive to Active
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC transforms the seller from a passive participant into an active manager of the mutual engagement timeline.

narrativeContexts.context: Decision Process addresses the mechanics of HOW the evaluation, selection, and approval will occur. Sellers who understand the evaluation criteria but not the process mechanics face deal slippage from unexpected steps, unfamiliar stakeholders, or longer timelines than anticipated.

The seller maps the complete end-to-end decision methodology including all stakeholders by name and role, establishes the timeline with specific dates, converts the decision process into a mutual action plan, and uses champion and EB relationships to manage the timeline.

Common pitfalls include treating the decision process as a seller-only tracking document, mapping the process at a single point without updating, failing to identify all stakeholders, neglecting regular cadence meetings, and missing the connection between decision process and paper process management.

narratives.name: Proactive Paper Process Management Across Four Sub-Domains
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC structures paper process navigation across contracting, procurement, legal, and budget dimensions.

narrativeContexts.context: Paper process surprises are among the most common causes of deal slippage. The MEDDPICC Overview identifies four sub-domains: Contracting, Procurement, Legal and Compliance, and Budget and Finance. Each has its own stakeholders, requirements, and potential delays.

Paper Process management requires proactive engagement across all four sub-domains. The seller establishes procurement contacts, maps contracting policies and legal requirements, identifies timing risks proactively, sequences multi-party signatures, and anticipates legal review by sharing draft agreements.

Common pitfalls include treating paper process as a late-stage reactive activity, failing to identify timing risks until they cause delays, assuming standard PO timelines, neglecting partner procurement requirements, and not sending draft agreements proactively to anticipate legal review.

narratives.name: Three-Category Competitive Assessment and Counter-Positioning
narratives.description: How MEDDPICC structures competitive analysis across external vendors, in-house development, and organizational inertia.

narrativeContexts.context: MEDDPICC defines competition expansively: other vendors bidding for the deal, the customer developing in-house, and the customer choosing to do nothing. The quality rubric warns against assuming Red Hat is clearly superior and favored, characterizing this as dangerous overconfidence.

Competitive assessment follows a structured approach across all three categories. External vendors are identified with specific products and capabilities. In-house development capability is assessed including opportunity cost. The do-nothing option is analyzed for escalating consequences. Resources from Competitive Insights, Sales Plays, and Product Business Units are engaged.

Evidence-based competitive positioning transforms the quality of the competitive narrative from assumed superiority to specific, numbered advantages tied to customer pain points. Champion validation ensures the narrative resonates internally. Partner competitive intelligence enriches the picture beyond what direct engagement reveals.

narratives.name: From Status Updates to Targeted Coaching Interventions
narratives.description: How AI-augmented deal reviews transform coaching from time-consuming full reviews to focused, high-impact sessions.

narrativeContexts.context: Traditional deal reviews often devolve into status updates that consume time without driving qualification improvement. The shift from manual preparation and full 8-letter reviews to AI-augmented focused reviews covering 2-3 prioritized letters represents a fundamental change in coaching methodology.

The deal review integrates three activities: scoring assessment, structured coaching, and AI-augmented preparation. Before the meeting the manager reviews and defines objectives. During the meeting the structured agenda covers overview, deep dive, action items, and coaching. After the meeting action items are documented and progress is monitored.

Common pitfalls include conducting reviews without structured preparation, allowing reviews to become status updates, failing to document action items with owners, treating AI priorities as definitive rather than validating them, and neglecting post-meeting follow-up where coaching impact actually materializes.

patterns.name: MEDDPICC Qualification Journey
patterns.description: End-to-end opportunity qualification lifecycle aligned to Red Hat sales stages.

narratives.name: Qualification Lifecycle from Discovery to Expansion
narratives.description: The end-to-end MEDDPICC qualification progression through six phases of the sales engagement journey.

narrativeContexts.context: The MEDDPICC Qualification Journey begins when a potential opportunity has been recognized and entered into the pipeline. At this stage the account team initiates the MEDDPICC Scorecard and begins structured pain discovery to establish the foundation for all subsequent qualification dimensions. The focus is on understanding who is experiencing challenges, what approaches have failed, and whether the opportunity warrants organizational investment.

As qualification deepens, the account team systematically addresses all eight MEDDPICC dimensions with increasing rigor. Pain is quantified, the value case is built using the Business Value Framework, the champion's influence is confirmed, the Economic Buyer is engaged, decision criteria are shaped, the decision process is mapped, competitive threats are assessed, and the scorecard achieves comprehensive coverage with Proficient quality responses supported by structured deal review coaching.

With validation complete, the account team shifts focus to commercial execution. The value proposition is compelling and customer-validated, the champion operates as a power broker with EB influence, and the decision timeline is actively managed through key relationships. A mutual close plan with agreed milestones provides the execution framework while the scorecard meets pipeline governance requirements.

Active negotiation leverages the full qualification intelligence built through the MEDDPICC framework. The Economic Buyer remains actively engaged throughout, competitive positioning is defended with evidence-based arguments, and the paper process is managed across contracting, procurement, legal, and budget sub-domains. Timing risks including holidays, PTO, and multi-party signature sequences are proactively managed.

Deal closure executes the mutual close plan with every step tracked to completion. The comprehensive MEDDPICC Scorecard provides a complete intelligence package for post-sale handoff. Paper process management ensures all contracting, procurement, and signature requirements are fulfilled. The qualification trajectory documented through progressive deal reviews evidences the systematic improvement that drove the deal to successful conclusion.

The won opportunity generates follow-on expansion potential informed by the deep customer intelligence accumulated through MEDDPICC qualification. Growth opportunities surfaced during deal reviews, value realization tracking that validates the original business case, and coaching learnings that improve organizational selling behavior all contribute to the expansion cycle, and the MEDDPICC framework is applied to new expansion opportunities with the same structured discipline.
